item.title: Union pushes for health Insurance, safe mining and environmental accountability
item.description: The Zimbabwe Diamond and Allied Workers Union (ZDAMWU) has called for urgent reforms in the mining sector, including compulsory health insurance for workers, stronger safety standards and stricter environmental rehabilitation measures.

item.title: High rents price small traders out of partitioned shops
item.description: Informal traders in Bulawayo say soaring rents for newly partitioned shops are pushing them out of formal trading spaces and back onto the streets, undermining efforts to decongest the city.

item.title: Where is the sugar tax going? MPs press govt over cancer funding
item.description: The government has been challenged to explain how millions of dollars collected through a tax on sugar-sweetened beverages are being used, amid concerns that cancer treatment services remain in a critical state.

item.title: ​Why is it that every constitutional change since 2013 has ignored the people and only served the elite?
item.description: It becomes problematic when the hunger to consolidate power become more powerful that the hunger to uplift citizens.

item.title: Zimbabwe remains among the world’s most corrupt nations while the elite amend the constitution to protect their looting
item.description: How does the protection of looting end up being framed as the national interest?

item.title: War veterans faction demands immediate dialogue on Constitution Amendment Bill
item.description: Afaction of the Zimbabwe National Liberation War Veterans Association (ZNLWVA) has called for an immediate national dialogue over the proposed Constitution of Zimbabwe Amendment Bill, warning that no constitutional change that weakens democratic accountability or sidesteps popular approval can claim moral or historical legitimacy.

item.title: Traders support stricter penalties to stop city littering
item.description: Bulawayo residents and traders are backing tougher enforcement of anti-litter laws following a recent city-wide clean-up campaign, calling for higher fines to discourage illegal dumping and maintain public cleanliness.

item.title: Zimbabwe’s “2030” constitutional push: why now, who’s behind it, who resists, and how likely it is to pass
item.description: Zimbabwe’s Cabinet has approved a Constitutional Amendment Bill (2026) that would (1) extend presidential and parliamentary terms from five to seven years and replace direct presidential elections with a parliamentary election of the president.

item.description: ‘I have faith that Zimbabwe will be found through the mobilisation and action of its patriotic children’

item.title: Zimbabwe grapples with shortages of birth certificates and ID papers
item.description: Zimbabwe is grappling with a growing shortage of critical materials needed to print birth certificates, national Identity Documents (IDs) and official receipt books, raising concerns over access to essential civil registration services.
